·  Mallorca, for two
The plan Palma Pollença Black book
An itinerary for two

Mallorca

A leisurely fortnight of cute dates, slow sundowners and turquoise coves.

When
2 – 14 July 2026
Nights
4 in Palma · 8 up north
Bases
Abelay Hotel · Hotel Uyal
Wheels
Hire car from 6 July
Begin

Two cities, two tempos, and the whole island in between — built so you fit the good stuff in without ever feeling rushed.

The first four nights belong to Palma — café mornings, a cathedral, rooftop sundowners and the bars and beach clubs you flagged, all on foot or a short taxi. No car, no fuss.

Then you pick up the hire car and head north to Port de Pollença for eight slow days of coves, mountain drives and long lunches, using the bay as your basecamp.

Every day leaves room to do nothing — a swim, a siesta, an unplanned hour. The big drives are spaced out, with a gentler day either side.

Good to know
Peak July: book the romantic tables early Heat: beaches & drives early or late Formentor: car-free by day — take the bus Markets: Alcúdia Tue · Pollença Sun Pack: a little cash & swim shoes

02

Five golden rules

01

Book the headliners now

July is peak. The romantic tables — El Olivo, Ca’s Patró March, Sa Foradada, Cap Rocat — fill weeks ahead.

02

Beat the heat

Beaches and mountain drives early or late. Midday (30°C+) is for long lunches, shade and a siesta.

03

Two bases, two tempos

Palma is walkable city nights — no car needed. The north is car-and-cove days.

04

Formentor by bus

The lighthouse road is car-free by day in summer. Let Bus 334 do the driving and skip the parking scrum.

05

Cash & swim shoes

A few coves are cash-only and pebbly. Pack a little of both and you’re never caught out.

Book these before you fly

  • El Olivo, Deià — book well ahead
  • Ca’s Patró March, Cala Deià — and bring cash
  • Sa Foradada — sunset slots vanish

Chapter One
I

Palma

Abelay Hotel · Thu 2 – Mon 6 July · on foot

Day 02 · Thursday, 2 July

Touchdown & a first stroll

You land at 19:30, so tonight is a gentle one: drop the bags, amble into the old town, and let one easy dinner ease you in. Everything is a short walk from the Abelay.

  • 19:30
    Touch down

    A taxi has you at the Abelay in ~15–20 min. Drop the bags, freshen up.

  • 20:45
    Dinner close to baseStill to book

    Stroll 8 min down Carrer de Sant Miquel to Buscando El Norte — relaxed, generous tapas, open late. (Origen Tapas on Plaça de la Ferreria is a lovely alternative, ~14 min.)

  • 22:15
    A floodlit wander

    Carry on to the lit-up Plaça Major and dip into the old-town lanes. A gentle loop back, then an early night.

Day 03 · Friday, 3 July

Cala Comtessa & Santa Catalina

Stay close to the city today — an easy bus down to a turquoise Illetes cove for a long, lazy swim, then back to buzzy Santa Catalina for dinner, cocktails and — if you fancy — a dance.

  • LATE MORN
    A lazy start

    No rush — you’re staying close to the city today.

  • 12:00
    Cala Comtessa

    EMT Bus 4 to the Ses Illetes terminus (~35–40 min, every ~10 min), then a short walk to a small turquoise cove looking out to a little islet — swim out to it if you fancy. Go earlyish; it fills in July. Bigger & easier: Cala Major on Bus 3.

  • 14:00
    A long beach lunch

    Feet in the sand, no agenda.

  • 16:30
    Back & reset

    Bus back to the city, rinse off and change for the evening.

  • 20:30
    Dinner at Azuca✓ Booked

    Your booking — Azuca, a lively urban bistro with brilliant energy. (If plans shift, Duke for creative small plates or OSMA for refined French are right nearby.)

  • DRINK
    CocktailsStill to book

    Quentin’s Saloon — speakeasy, serious drinks. LAB and Agabar — craft cocktails and agave, buzzing till late.

  • DANCE
    Boogie

    Santa Catalina is bars; the clubs sit 5–10 min south on the Paseo Marítimo — La Bodeguita del Medio (Cuban/salsa) and Thalassa Marítimo (Latin/reggaeton), or Garito Café for DJ sets.

Day 04 · Saturday, 4 July

Cove, rooftop & old town

A lie-in, a turquoise swim, then a golden-hour rooftop, your El Camino booking and a proper old-town night out.

A note on sunset & your booking

In early July the sun sets ~21:25 — just as your El Camino table (21:30) begins. So take the long golden hour from the rooftop first (it’s gorgeous from ~20:00), then it’s a 10-min walk down to dinner. You’ll catch the glow, just not the final dip.

  • LIE-IN
    Slow morning

    No alarm. A late brunch near the hotel if you surface slowly.

  • 12:30
    A turquoise swim

    To Cala Major today — you did Cala Comtessa yesterday. EMT Bus 3 from the centre (~20–25 min) drops you at an easy, sandy town beach with calm, shallow water and a couple of beach bars for lunch.

  • 16:30
    Back & reset

    Bus back, rinse off, change for the evening.

  • 20:00
    Golden-hour rooftop drinks✓ Booked

    Your booking — sundowners at Es Príncep’s rooftop, with sea on one side and the old town and cathedral on the other.

  • 21:30
    Dinner at El Camino✓ Booked

    Your booking — counter-seat tapas, lively and excellent. About 10 min walk from the rooftop.

  • 23:00
    Bar Abaco

    Into La Lonja for cocktails amid the baroque candlelight and piled fruit.

  • LATE
    Dance it out

    Lively bars line Carrer dels Apuntadors in La Lonja; for a real boogie, the Paseo Marítimo clubs (Garito Café, Thalassa, La Bodeguita) are a short walk or taxi along the water.

Day 05 · Sunday, 5 July

Cathedral, palace & sushi

Another lie-in, a cathedral-view breakfast, the royal palace next door, a lazy old-town wander, then sushi near the hotel and an early night.

  • LIE-IN
    Slow start

    Sleep in — you’ve earned a quiet day.

  • 10:30
    Breakfast with a view

    Cappuccino at Palau March (Carrer del Conquistador) — a terrace looking straight at the cathedral and Almudaina. Avocado toast and good coffee.

  • 12:00
    Royal Palace of La Almudaina

    Tour the royal palace right beside the cathedral — courtyards, the Gothic chapel, sea-facing ramparts (~1 hr). Open Tue–Sun.

  • 16:00
    Casco antiguo & La Lonja

    Wander the old town and the Born for a browse. Heads up: most shops shut on Sundays, but the Born and old-town tourist boutiques and galleries stay open — more of a stroll than a spree.

  • 19:00
    Back to change

    To the hotel to freshen up.

  • 19:30
    Sushi near base✓ Booked

    Your booking — Daikiya (Carrer del General Riera, ~10 min walk), top-notch sushi and dim sum. (For a fancier omakase, Izakaya is ~20 min toward Santa Catalina.)

  • EARLY
    An early night

    A nightcap if you like — then rest up for the drive north tomorrow.

Day 06 · Monday, 6 July

The Sóller tram, then north

Collect the car and take the long way to your second base — up to Sóller, down to the sea on the vintage tram, then on to the bay at Port de Pollença.

The tram & the drive on

The open-sided 1913 vintage tram runs from beside the Sóller train station down to Port de Sóller every ~30 min (buy tickets at the stop); park in Sóller around the town or station. Afterwards it’s about 1 h 15 on to Port de Pollença — easiest back through the Ma-11 tunnel and up the motorway. The coastal Ma-10 over the mountains is glorious but slow, so you might save that for the Sa Calobra day.

  • 09:30
    Checkout & collect the car

    Check out of the Abelay; a quick taxi to the airport to pick up the hire car.

  • 10:30
    Drive to Sóller

    ~45 min around Palma and up through the Ma-11 tunnel into the Sóller valley; park near the town.

  • 11:30
    Tram to Port de Sóller

    Ride the vintage tram down through the orange groves to the seafront (~30 min).

  • 12:30
    Port de Sóller

    A long harbour lunch and a swim in the sheltered bay; stroll the promenade.

  • 15:30
    Tram back, then north

    Tram back to Sóller, then on to Port de Pollença (~1 h 15) — easiest through the tunnel and up the motorway.

  • 17:30
    Settle in at Hotel Uyal

    Right on the bay, on the Pine Walk — home for the next eight nights.

  • 19:00
    Passeig Voramar stroll

    Tamarisk shade, glassy water, the Tramuntana glowing.

  • 21:00
    Dinner on the frontStill to book

    Stay, out on the jetty, is the classic.

Chapter Two
II

Port de Pollença

Hotel Uyal · Mon 6 – Tue 14 July · by car

Day 07 · Tuesday, 7 July

Turquoise & the home patch

Ease into the north with a short hop to the gem-coloured coves of Cala Sant Vicenç, then your nearest hill town and dinner under the planes of Pollença’s old square.

  • 10:30
    Cala Sant Vicenç

    A 12-min drive to a cluster of jewel coves — Cala Molins for the easy sandy swim, Cala Barques for the drama.

  • 14:00
    Lunch by the cove

    Feet in the sand at Cala Molins.

  • 17:00
    Pollença old town

    Climb the 365 cypress-lined Calvari steps for the view, then wander down into Plaça Major.

  • 21:00
    Dinner in PollençaStill to book

    Under the planes on Plaça Major — Can 1907 (Mediterranean plates and cocktails, often live music) or Anima e Farina for superb Italian focaccia and pizza. A nightcap at U Gallet by the Calvari steps or Oh Vermut just off the square.

Day 08 · Wednesday, 8 July

Sa Calobra & the gorge

A big Tramuntana day: the hairpin ‘tie-knot’ road down to the sea, then a walk through sea-carved tunnels to the dramatic mouth of the Torrent de Pareis canyon.

The road down

The final 12 km to Sa Calobra coil through famous hairpins, including the 360° ‘nus de sa corbata’ (tie-knot). Take them slowly and set off earlyish to beat the coach tours; there’s a car park at the bottom. Boat trips also run from Port de Sóller and Can Picafort if you’d rather skip the drive entirely.

  • 09:00
    Drive to Sa Calobra

    ~1 h 15 over the mountains; the coil of hairpins at the end is part of the fun.

  • 11:00
    Through the tunnels

    From the cove, walk the short footpath through two old rock tunnels to the boulder beach where the gorge meets the sea.

  • 12:00
    Swim at the gorge mouth

    Clear, deep water between towering canyon walls. Water shoes help on the pebbles.

  • 14:00
    Lunch by the cove

    A simple bite at Sa Calobra before the drive back.

  • 20:30
    Relaxed dinner in the portStill to book

    An easy night back on the bay after the big drive — book a seafront table.

Day 09 · Thursday, 9 July

Long beach & Alcúdia old town

An easy day close to home — kilometres of soft sand on the bay, then the honey-stone lanes of Alcúdia’s old town and dinner inside the walls.

  • 11:00
    Playa de Muro

    A 15-min drive to one of the island’s best beaches — fine white sand and warm, shallow turquoise water that runs on for miles.

  • 14:00
    Beach-club lunchOPTIONAL

    Feet-in-sand tables at NU on Playa de Muro — sushi, cocktails and a DJ easing the afternoon along (or any of the simple beach balnearios).

  • 19:30
    Alcúdia old town

    Wander the floodlit medieval ramparts and the lanes inside the Porta del Moll gate.

  • 21:00
    Dinner in the old townStill to book

    Celler Ca’n Costa — Alcúdia’s oldest restaurant, classic Mallorcan (the rabbit and the paella are the things) — or Merlet, beautiful modern tapas by the gate. Cocktails after at Bodega Ca’n Pantina.

Day 10 · Friday, 10 July

A bay day, then Deià

Stay local by the bay today — sea, sand and a slow lunch on the front — then drive into the mountains as the light softens for drinks in Deià village and dinner at El Olivo.

  • MORN
    The Vall de Bóquer walk

    From the edge of the port, walk up into the dramatic Bóquer Valley — a famous birdwatchers’ gorge — to the wild little cove of Cala Bóquer (about 45 min each way). Prefer it lazy? A morning on the town beach instead.

  • 13:00
    Lunch on the front

    A long, easy seafront lunch — Bucca for sea views and good plates, or a marina table.

  • AFT
    Pool & siesta

    Back to the hotel for the pool and a rest before the evening.

  • 18:30
    Into Deià

    Drive up the coast (~1 h 10) as the heat eases; park and wander the steep, honey-stone lanes.

  • 19:30
    Drinks in the villageStill to book

    A cocktail at bohemian Sa Fonda (live music, a Deià institution) or stylish Barracó with its valley view — or arrive early at La Residencia for a drink on the Café Miró terrace.

  • 21:30
    Dinner at El OlivoStill to book

    The romantic finale — candlelit fine dining on the terrace at Belmond La Residencia.

Day 11 · Saturday, 11 July

Formentor by bus

The peninsula at the island’s tip — cliffs, a lighthouse and a pine-shaded swim, with the bus doing the hard driving so you don’t have to.

Heads up — the Formentor road

From 15 May–18 Oct the Ma-2210 to Formentor is closed to hire cars 10:00–22:00. Easiest plan: hop on Bus 334 from Port de Pollença (~50 min to the lighthouse), stopping at Mirador es Colomer, Platja de Formentor and Cala Figuera — tickets on the bus, pay by card. Or drive out before 10:00 to park at the beach for an early swim (you still can’t drive on to the lighthouse). A boat trip from the port is a third lovely option.

  • 10:30
    Bus 334 from the port

    Hop on in Port de Pollença and sit back for the cliff-edge ride.

  • 11:00
    Mirador es Colomer

    The island’s most photographed viewpoint — a short clifftop path.

  • 11:45
    The lighthouse

    Land’s end, all sea and sky.

  • 13:00
    Swim at Formentor

    Down to pine-backed Platja de Formentor (or quieter Cala Figuera) for an afternoon under the trees.

  • 20:00
    Sundowners & dinner in the portStill to book

    Back in the port for a drink by the water and a relaxed seafront dinner.

Day 12 · Sunday, 12 July

Cala Mesquida & the dunes

A wilder beach day out to the northeast — a broad sweep of sand backed by protected dunes and pine, with big open water and room to breathe.

  • 10:30
    Drive to Cala Mesquida

    ~45 min northeast, near Capdepera.

  • 11:30
    The dune beach

    A wide, wild beach behind rolling dunes — wonderful for a long swim; it can pick up a breeze and a little surf.

  • 14:00
    Lunch

    Simple beach-bar fare, or back in pretty Capdepera.

  • 16:00
    Cala Gat, if you likeOPTIONAL

    Ten minutes on at Cala Ratjada — a pine-fringed cove by the lighthouse for a second dip.

  • 20:30
    Easy eveningStill to book

    A relaxed dinner back near the bay (or stop in Alcúdia old town on the way home).

Day 13 · Monday, 13 July

A slow day on the bay

Your last full day, kept gentle and local — no long drive, just the bay. A few easy ways to spend it, then a special seafront table for the final night.

  • ON THE WATER
    Boat trip or paddleOPTIONAL

    Hire a SUP or kayak on the calm bay, or take a little boat trip from the port around the headlands and into quiet coves.

  • ON THE SAND
    A lazy beach dayOPTIONAL

    Stretch out on the Port de Pollença town beach — gentle, shallow water, with beach bars right behind you.

  • ON FOOT
    Cycle or potterOPTIONAL

    Spin along the flat bayfront cycle path, browse the little shops, and take an afternoon coffee in the sun.

  • 13:00
    Lunch by the sea

    Feet-near-the-sand at Llaüt Beach Bar, or a long lunch at Embat on the front.

  • 21:00
    A last-night seafront tableStill to book

    Make it special: Stay out on the jetty, sea-view Vista, romantic top-rated No 31, or cosy Ca’n Panxo for the island’s best paella.

Day 14 · Tuesday, 14 July

One last swim, then home

A slow morning by the water, a final lunch, and an easy run south to the airport.

  • MORN
    A final swim

    Off the Pine Walk, or a dawn-quiet Cala de Sant Vicenç.

  • 11:00
    Checkout

    Store the bags if you need to.

  • 13:00
    Drive south & lunch

    ~1 hr to Palma; the airport’s 10 min from the city, so squeeze in a last lunch and wander (or linger in Alcúdia).

  • 17:00
    Return the car

    Be airside with plenty of buffer in peak season.

  • 20:25
    Flight home

    Hasta pronto, Mallorca. ✈
